GitHub.desc: Official GitHub app: explore repositories, read code, follow issues and pull requests, and get notifications. Very handy for finding an app's APK in its Releases section.

Komi Store.desc: Free, open source store with releases from GitHub, Codeberg and Forgejo that you can install with one tap. It helps you discover new apps, manage the ones you installed, and offers collections, update alerts and 14 languages. It used to be called GitHub Store.

F-Droid.desc: Catalog of free apps built from their source code. Apps update from within the app itself, and it warns you if any of them include ads or tracking.

Droid-ify.desc: Modern client for F-Droid and other repositories (like IzzyOnDroid): Material interface, search, installation and update alerts for free apps. Open source (GPL-3.0).

Aurora Store.desc: Alternative Google Play client: download apps from the Play catalog without signing in with your account and without Google services. It's open source and respects your privacy.

LibreFind.desc: Scans the apps installed on your phone, detects the closed-source ones and suggests free alternatives. It shows a «sovereignty» score (free vs. proprietary), and the community can vote and suggest alternatives. It only queries its database when it finds proprietary apps.

ShizuCoreFetch.desc: App store that uses Shizuku to install, uninstall and update apps at system level, without root. Browse a curated repository with screenshots, descriptions and version history, plus a local APK wallet, update alerts and 9 languages. Developers can list their apps with a shizu_store.json file. Open source (GPL-3.0). Android 8+.

IzzyOnDroid.desc: Unofficial client for the IzzyOnDroid free app repository: Material interface with your accent color, light and dark themes, categories, built-in APK installer and update alerts. Open source (GPL-3.0). Android 7+.
IzzyOnDroid.tip: Be careful: check apps before installing them.

Universal Installer.desc: Installs APK, APKS, XAPK and APKM files (with their OBB). It checks each file with VirusTotal (you can use your own key), lets you see the permissions it asks for and, with Shizuku, installs silently. It helps you avoid malware.

Obtainium.desc: Installs and updates apps straight from their author's releases page (GitHub and others), without going through a store. You paste the app's link and it tells you when a new version comes out. Open source (GPLv3). Android 8+.
Obtainium.tip: A great companion to Komi Store: use it for apps that only publish their APK on GitHub.

Shizuku.desc: Lets other apps use system features that normally require root or ADB, without rooting or losing your warranty. With wireless debugging (Android 11+) it's activated from the phone itself. This fork adds start on boot, automatic restart if it crashes and a stealth mode.
Shizuku.tip: Heads up: its developer said they have paused maintenance for now.

ShizukuPlus.desc: Improved version of the Shizuku fork, with a different package so it can live alongside the original. It combines root, ADB and Dhizuku (Device Owner) modes and adds an activity log, bulk permission management, a «Service Doctor» for startup failures, and fixes for Android 16/17 and OneUI 8+. Open source (Apache-2.0). Android 7+.
ShizukuPlus.tip: Apps that look for the original Shizuku may need its compatibility mode.

Dhizuku.desc: Gives other apps Device Owner permissions without root, similar to what Shizuku does. Komi Store uses it to install apps without asking you for confirmation. Open source.
Dhizuku.tip: It's activated with an ADB command and, on many phones, you have to remove your accounts first.

LADB.desc: Terminal with local ADB: turn on wireless debugging and run ADB commands without connecting your phone to a computer. It's useful, for example, to start Shizuku. Open source (GPL-3.0).
LADB.tip: Needs Wi-Fi and wireless debugging turned on; sometimes you have to reconnect it after restarting.

Canta.desc: Removes or disables system apps you don't use (bloatware) without root, thanks to Shizuku. It classifies each app by risk (recommended, advanced, expert or unsafe) and lets you reinstall the ones you removed.
Canta.tip: Needs Shizuku. Removing system apps can cause problems: check ADL first and don't touch the ones marked as unsafe.

ADL.desc: Android Debloat List: an always-available wiki about Android's preinstalled apps. Search by name or package to find out whether you can remove an app before doing it with Canta. Each page has a link to open it in App Manager.
ADL.tip: It's a website, so it needs internet. Check it before removing anything with Canta so you don't damage your phone.

App Manager.desc: Advanced, free app manager: view and block components (activities, services…), detect trackers and permissions, install and export APKs, and make backups. It works without root and does more with root or ADB. Open source (GPL-3.0).
App Manager.tip: Blocking components can break apps: do it carefully.

App Ops.desc: Controls each app's permissions in more detail than Android's regular settings (AppOps), including some that the system hides. It works with Shizuku.
App Ops.tip: Needs Shizuku. Changing system permissions can make some apps fail.

Inure.desc: Very complete app manager: lists installed or uninstalled apps, lets you view and tweak their internal components, and comes with a terminal, usage statistics, a split-APK installer, VirusTotal and tools to remove bloatware. It works with root or Shizuku. Open source (GPL-3.0) with Material You themes.
Inure.tip: It has a 15-day trial; after that it's unlocked with its full version.

SD Maid SE.desc: Cleans junk files, leftovers from uninstalled apps and duplicates, and analyzes what's taking up your storage. It cleans more deeply with root, Shizuku or ADB. Open source (GPL-3.0).
SD Maid SE.tip: Some features are paid. Check carefully what you're about to delete before confirming.

Essentials.desc: Many features in a single app: app locking, per-app night light, screen refresh rate control, freezing apps, automations and screen customization, such as the floating island. It asks for deep permissions and some features use Shizuku.

AutoPie.desc: Command center and automations: run shell and Python scripts with a simple interface, with a built-in Termux. They can be launched manually, from Share, when a file appears, on a schedule, or with a shortcut or widget. It comes with a catalog of ready-made commands. Open source (Apache-2.0).
AutoPie.tip: Only works on arm64 phones (most recent ones). For scheduled tasks, turn off battery optimization for the app.

Termux.desc: Terminal for Android with a Linux environment: you install packages with apt (Python, git, SSH, compilers…) and work from the command line without root. Open source (GPL-3.0). Android 7+.
Termux.tip: Install it from F-Droid and don't mix sources: its add-ons require the same signature. It asks for many sensitive permissions.

scrcpy.desc: Shows and controls your Android from the computer over USB or Wi-Fi, without root and without installing anything on the phone. It works on Windows, macOS and Linux. Open source (Apache-2.0).
scrcpy.tip: Needs USB debugging turned on on the phone and is used from the PC.

Plain.desc: Control your phone from another device's browser over the local network: files, photos, videos, music and more, without the cloud. Open source.
Plain.tip: It asks for many permissions (files, contacts…): give it only the ones you use and use it on a network you trust.

Neo Backup.desc: Back up and restore your apps, their data and their settings, with encryption and automatic scheduling. Open source (GPL-3.0).
Neo Backup.tip: To back up apps' data it needs root.

EnforceDoze.desc: Forces Doze mode as soon as the screen turns off (or after a delay) to save battery, disables motion sensors and lets you manage the Doze whitelist. It's a fork of ForceDoze, which is no longer maintained. It works without root and gains options with root. Open source (GPL-3.0). Android 6+.

No More Background.desc: Shows all your apps on a single screen and you choose which ones can run in the background, to save battery and data. It works with ADB, Shizuku or root; you set it up once and that's it, with no need to «optimize» every day.
No More Background.tip: Some apps may keep running in the background even if you turn them off.

BatStats.desc: Battery monitor with advanced statistics, such as per-app consumption in mAh. To see everything you need Shizuku, root or to grant four permissions via ADB. Open source (GPL-3.0).
BatStats.tip: Some detailed data isn't available on all phones.

Extinguish.desc: Really turns the screen off (it doesn't just put a black layer over it) and keeps the phone awake so other apps keep working, for example when listening to videos. It works on LCD and OLED and saves battery. It's controlled with a floating button, volume keys, tap, notification, quick setting or ADB. Open source (GPL-3.0).
Extinguish.tip: On phones modified by the manufacturer it may not work well. Know in advance how to turn the screen back on.

Display Toggle.desc: Turns the physical screen off and on without locking the phone or stopping open apps. It includes shortcuts and a quick setting. Open source (MIT). Android 7+.

OrientationLock.desc: Forces the screen orientation (portrait, landscape, automatic…) even if an app won't let you rotate it.

FireWall Blocks.desc: Lets you remove Wi-Fi or mobile data access app by app, to cut connections you don't need.

PrivacyFlip.desc: When you lock your phone it turns off Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, data, location, NFC and even camera and microphone (Android 12+); when you unlock it, it turns back on only what you choose. It has «only if not in use» modes, works with Shizuku or root and sends no telemetry.

Alternate.desc: Identifies who's calling you with a local database, without passing those numbers to your contacts or your messaging apps. It stores numbers temporarily, validates phone numbers by country, has biometric lock and imports or exports VCF contacts. Open source (MIT), with no ads or trackers. Android 7+.
Alternate.tip: It asks for access to the call log and to display over other apps. arm64 only.

Exodus.desc: Shows which trackers and permissions each app installed on your phone has, using the reports from the εxodus platform, by the French nonprofit Exodus Privacy. Very useful for checking apps before trusting them. Open source (GPL-3.0). Android 6+.

Bitwarden.desc: Stores your passwords and passkeys in an end-to-end encrypted vault and syncs them across your devices. It generates strong passwords, autofills, supports two-step verification and has Bitwarden Send to share data securely. It's free and open source, with an optional Premium plan.

SnapSafe.desc: Camera that saves photos encrypted in the app's private storage and has no internet permission. It has a gallery with a separate PIN, removes metadata when sharing, blurs faces and lets you choose which location to add. It includes a decoy PIN that deletes your photos when used. Open source (MIT).
SnapSafe.tip: Photos live only inside the app and aren't included in backups: save separately the ones you want to keep.

Tarnhelm.desc: Cleans the tracking parameters from links you share from other apps, seamlessly. Open source (GPL-3.0). Android 8.1+.
Tarnhelm.tip: It asks for several permissions (display over other apps, auto-start): check them when you install.

Fake Traveler.desc: Changes your GPS location to any point on the map. It's activated by choosing it as the «mock location app» in Developer options. Open source (GPL-3.0).
Fake Traveler.tip: Some apps detect fake locations and may restrict your account: use it carefully.

Orbot.desc: Routes the traffic of the apps you choose (or of the whole phone) through the Tor network using a local VPN, with bridges for areas with censorship. Made by Guardian Project. Open source.

TrackerControl.desc: A local firewall (via VPN) that detects and blocks the trackers in your apps and shows you which companies and servers each one talks to. No root or accounts needed. Open source (GPL-3.0).

AirGuard.desc: Alerts you if a Bluetooth tracker (AirTag, Find My, SmartTag or similar) is following you without your knowledge and helps you find it. It is a research project from the SEEMOO lab (TU Darmstadt). Open source.

Shelter.desc: Creates an Android work profile so you can install apps in isolation, clone apps (two accounts on one phone) and “freeze” the ones you don't use. Open source.
Shelter.tip: Some ROMs (like MIUI) don't support the work profile well. It is not a total safe: it doesn't protect you from Android bugs.

Aegis Authenticator.desc: Stores your two-step verification (2FA) codes encrypted on your phone, without relying on anyone's cloud. Supports encrypted backups and fingerprint lock. Open source (GPLv3). Android 6+.
Aegis Authenticator.tip: Make an encrypted backup and keep it outside your phone: if you lose the phone, without it you lose your codes.

Signal.desc: Private messaging with end-to-end encryption by default: chats, voice notes, calls and video calls (groups of up to 1,000 people and group calls of up to 50). It has disappearing messages and 24-hour stories. It is open source, ad-free and funded by donations.
Signal.tip: To sign up it needs a phone number; afterwards you can hide it from others with a username in Settings.

Session.desc: Private, open-source messaging that doesn't ask for a phone number or email: you sign up with just an account ID. Its messages travel through a decentralized network with onion routing, designed to protect your IP and who you talk to. It has chats, groups, communities of over 100 people and temporary messages, and it doesn't collect or sell your data.
Session.tip: Your account is saved with a recovery phrase: write it down somewhere safe, because without it the account can't be recovered.

Molly.desc: An alternative version of Signal with extra security: it encrypts the local database with a passphrase, wipes sensitive data from memory and can work without Google services. It uses the Signal network. Open source (AGPL-3.0).
Molly.tip: It is a project independent from Signal, although it uses the same network and account.

Element (Matrix).desc: A Matrix client: end-to-end encrypted chats, groups and video calls on an open, decentralized network. You can choose a server or host your own. Open source.

Proton Mail.desc: End-to-end encrypted email from Proton (Switzerland), with a limited free plan. The app is open source.
Proton Mail.tip: The app is open source, but the service can't be self-hosted. If it doesn't show up in Komi Store, use its official website.

Tuta Mail.desc: End-to-end encrypted email, calendar and contacts with a free plan. The app is open source.
Tuta Mail.tip: If it doesn't show up in Komi Store, use its official website.

Image Toolbox.desc: A very complete image editor: over 500 filters, conversion between formats (JPEG, PNG, WEBP, AVIF, HEIC, JXL…), cropping, drawing, background removal, watermarks, collages, EXIF editing, OCR in over 120 languages, PDF tools and AI tools for upscaling and denoising. Free and open source (Apache-2.0).
Image Toolbox.tip: The FOSS version has no analytics; the Play version does.

DeJPEG.desc: Removes compression artifacts, noise and backgrounds from your photos offline, using ONNX models that you download once (FBCNN, SCUNet, RMBG). It has a before/after comparison and OLED, light, dark and dynamic themes. Open source (GPL-3.0). Android 8+.

Ente Photos.desc: End-to-end encrypted photo backup and albums, synced across your devices and shareable with whoever you want. This F-Droid version doesn't use Google services. Open source (AGPL-3.0).
Ente Photos.tip: Needs internet and an account; the free space is limited.

TagSpaces.desc: Organize, tag and browse your files, photos and documents with no cloud or accounts. It stores tags in the file name or in sidecar files, searches with typo tolerance and includes viewers for images, PDF, Markdown, audio and video, plus notes and to-do lists. Open source (AGPL-3.0).
TagSpaces.tip: It asks for access to all storage, because it works as a file manager.

Gander.desc: Opens PDF, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, photos, video, audio, Markdown, text and code in a single app, with search inside documents. It asks for no permissions or internet, with no ads or accounts. Open source (MIT). Weighs about 15 MB. Android 8+.

Material Files.desc: An open-source file manager with Material design: internal storage, SD card, FTP, SFTP, SMB and WebDAV, compressed archives and a basic text editor. Open source (GPL-3.0).

Fossify Gallery.desc: An ad-free photo and video gallery: albums, filters, a basic editor, a trash bin and customizable colors. Open source (GPL-3.0).

Open Camera.desc: A free, ad-free camera with manual controls (ISO, exposure, focus), HDR, panorama, burst, stabilization and video in many resolutions. Open source (GPL-3.0+).
Open Camera.tip: It isn't on GitHub, so it doesn't show up in Komi Store.

Iceraven.desc: An unofficial browser based on Firefox (Fenix) with GeckoView. It adds about:config, tab suspending to save memory, hiding recent sites and less telemetry. It tries to install many more extensions than Firefox, although most don't work. MPL-2.0 license.
Iceraven.tip: No guarantees of security or updates: its APKs use a debug key, so treat it as alpha software.

LibreWolf.desc: A Firefox-based browser with hardened privacy and security: no telemetry and with uBlock Origin included. For Windows, macOS and Linux.
LibreWolf.tip: It's for computers: there is no official Android version.

RedReader.desc: A free, lightweight client for reading Reddit, with no ads. You can log in with your account or read without one. Open source (GPL-3.0).

LocalSend.desc: Sends files and messages to nearby devices over your Wi-Fi, with no internet, accounts or servers, and with encryption. Works on Android, iOS, Windows, macOS and Linux. Open source (Apache-2.0).
LocalSend.tip: The devices must be on the same Wi-Fi network.

NewPipe.desc: A lightweight, free client for watching YouTube without Google services or an account. It plays in the background and in a floating window, downloads video and audio and saves your subscriptions and playlists on your phone. It also opens SoundCloud, PeerTube and Bandcamp. Open source (GPL-3.0).
NewPipe.tip: It doesn't log in: your subscriptions are saved only on your phone and you can export them.

LibreTube.desc: An alternative YouTube client with no ads or Google account. It uses open-source servers instead of Google's and includes background playback, downloads, subscriptions and SponsorBlock. Open source (GPL-3.0).
LibreTube.tip: It depends on third-party public servers: if a video doesn't load, try another instance in Settings.

Seal.desc: A simple interface for yt-dlp with Material You design: downloads video and audio from lots of sites, grabs playlists with one tap, embeds subtitles, thumbnail and metadata and supports command templates. Open source (GPL-3.0).
Seal.tip: ⚠ It is barely maintained and YouTube downloads may fail. If it doesn't work for you, try YTDLnis.

YTDLnis.desc: A video and audio downloader based on yt-dlp: download queue and scheduling, playlists, custom commands, time-based cuts and background downloads. Open source (GPL-3.0).

AntennaPod.desc: A free, ad-free podcast player and manager: search and subscribe, download episodes, change the speed, set a sleep timer and sync your subscriptions with gpodder.net or Nextcloud. Open source (GPL-3.0).

Syncthing-Fork.desc: A wrapper for Syncthing on Android: syncs folders directly between your devices, with encryption and no cloud or accounts. Open source (MPL-2.0).
Syncthing-Fork.tip: The official Syncthing app for Android is discontinued; this fork is the one that keeps getting updates.

KDE Connect.desc: Connects your phone to your computer over the same network: you see notifications on the PC, share files and clipboard, control music and use your phone as a mouse and keyboard. Open source.
KDE Connect.tip: Both devices must be on the same Wi-Fi, and you need to install KDE Connect on the computer (or GSConnect on GNOME).

Tor Browser.desc: A Firefox-based browser that sends your traffic through the Tor network to hide your IP and protect your anonymity, blocks trackers and deletes cookies when you close it. Open source.
Tor Browser.tip: It is slower than a regular browser and some sites block it. On F-Droid it comes from the Guardian Project repository, which you need to add first.

Startpage.desc: A search engine that gives you Google results without tracking your activity; according to the company, it doesn't store your IP or your history. It has an anonymous view of pages and is used from the browser.
Startpage.tip: ⚠ It is closed source: you can't check how it protects your privacy. If you want something free and open, look at SearXNG.

SearXNG.desc: A free metasearch engine that gathers results from many search engines without tracking you or building a profile of you. You can use a public instance or set up your own. Open source (AGPL-3.0).
SearXNG.tip: Public instances are maintained by volunteers: choose a trustworthy one on searx.space.

CoMaps.desc: Maps and navigation based on OpenStreetMap that work without internet: you download regions, search for places and it guides you on foot, by bike or by car. No ads or tracking, and non-profit (Apache-2.0). It started as a fork of Organic Maps.
CoMaps.tip: Download the maps for your area over Wi-Fi before heading out.

Obsidian.desc: A Markdown note editor that stores everything as files on your phone and links your ideas together. It has community plugins and themes, and an optional sync that is paid separately. The app is free, but closed source.

My Brain.desc: A productivity app with tasks (priority, subtasks, reminders), Markdown notes, a mood journal, bookmarks, a calendar with a widget and an AI chat that can use your notes and tasks. It is local, collects no data and is open source (GPL-3.0). Android 8+.

Chrono.desc: A modern clock with highly configurable alarms (days, dates, ranges, ringtone, vibration, snooze and challenges like solving math problems or retyping text), world clocks, a timer with presets and a stopwatch with laps. It has Material You, customizable themes and backups. Open source (GPL-3.0). Android 5+.

LibreFit.desc: A workout log with exercises, sets, reps and duration, progress charts, customizable plans and over 800 exercises with instructions and images, filterable by equipment, muscle or difficulty. Works without internet and keeps your data on your phone. Open source (GPL-3.0).

SwitchAI.desc: Pick and switch between more than 40 AI assistants (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, DeepSeek…) from the system assistant gesture. You can choose one each time or set a default, with voice support, a widget and a quick setting. Open source (GPL-3.0). Android 8+.
SwitchAI.tip: It only launches the AI apps you already have installed.

Euria.desc: An AI assistant from Infomaniak (Switzerland): it writes, translates, proofreads, summarizes, transcribes audio, extracts text from images and searches the web. It organizes chats by project, syncs them and has an ephemeral mode that leaves no trace. The app is open source (GPL-3.0). Android 8+.
Euria.tip: Needs internet and an account (kSuite). Its service is not free software and it sends anonymous crash reports.

AnkiDroid.desc: Spaced-repetition flashcards for studying languages, your degree or anything you like. Imports decks, syncs with AnkiWeb and supports images, audio and LaTeX. Open source (GPL-3.0).

Markor.desc: A lightweight text and Markdown editor for notes, to-do lists and journaling, with preview and files that stay on your phone. Open source (Apache-2.0).

Breezy Weather.desc: Free, ad-free weather app with hourly and daily forecasts, alerts, air quality, pollen and widgets. You can choose between several data sources. Open source.

Tasks.org.desc: Free, ad-free task manager with reminders, lists, tags and subtasks. Syncs with CalDAV (like Nextcloud), Google Tasks or Microsoft To Do. Open source (GPL-3.0).

Fossify Calendar.desc: Simple, ad-free calendar with day, week, month and year views, reminders, repeating events, widgets and calendar syncing. Open source (GPL-3.0).

SeedlessDS.desc: Nintendo DS emulator designed for handheld consoles and dual-screen devices with physical buttons. It includes a library with cover art, save states, cheats, per-game settings, control layouts and RetroAchievements. It uses the proprietary DraStic core, so it is not fully free yet.
SeedlessDS.tip: It is in early beta and only works on arm64. It does not include games or BIOS files: use your own copies.

DroidDeck.desc: Runs Steam in Big Picture mode on Android and lets you play Windows games with Proton ARM64. It adds a Linux app store (Flathub), integrates GOG, Epic and Amazon Games, and does not need root. It is open source (GPL-3.0), a community creation with no relation to Valve.
DroidDeck.tip: It requires an Adreno 730 GPU or better (Mali, Xclipse and PowerVR do not work) and about 3 GB of free space.

Lemuroid.desc: Free emulator based on Libretro that covers NES, SNES, Game Boy, Genesis, N64, PlayStation, PSP, Nintendo DS and many more systems. It is easy to use: it scans your ROMs, saves and resumes games on its own, and has customizable touch controls, gamepad support, local multiplayer, cloud sync and Android TV support. Open source (GPL-3.0).
Lemuroid.tip: It does not include games: add your own ROMs.

Kimu X64.desc: A website to find games for your emulators, made by Kimu X64, a YouTube content creator who also talks about privacy, Linux on old computers and console modding. Tap «Credits» to go to their channel.

CatSmoker.desc: Optimizes supported games: it spoofs other phone models to unlock more graphics options and FPS, changes resolution and DPI, edits game configuration files, shows FPS, CPU, RAM and temperature, and includes an on-screen crosshair, a DNS optimizer and a game library. Works with root (Magisk, ZygiskNext and LSPosed) or with Shizuku. Android 8+.
CatSmoker.tip: Modifying files or faking your device may break the rules of some games and get you banned. The risk is yours.

Azahar.desc: Open-source Nintendo 3DS emulator for Android and PC, successor to Citra and Lime3DS: it raises the resolution, supports gamepads and saves states.
Azahar.tip: Only use games that you have copied from your own cartridges.

Dolphin.desc: GameCube and Wii emulator for Android and PC with resolution upgrades, gamepad support and quick save. Open source (GPL-2.0+).
Dolphin.tip: Only use games that you have copied from your own discs.

mGBA.desc: Fast and accurate Game Boy, Game Boy Color and Game Boy Advance emulator, with save states, filters and cheats. Open source (MPL-2.0).
mGBA.tip: Only use games that you have copied from your own cartridges.

PPSSPP.desc: PSP emulator for Android and PC: it raises the resolution, saves states and supports gamepads and cheats. Open source (GPL-2.0+).
PPSSPP.tip: On Google Play there is a paid Gold version; the free one is downloaded from its website.

Vita3K.desc: Experimental open-source PlayStation Vita emulator (GPLv2). It runs almost all homebrew and some commercial games.
Vita3K.tip: It is experimental and needs a powerful phone with Vulkan support; only use games that you have dumped from your own console.

GIF Live Wallpaper.desc: Use a GIF as an animated wallpaper. It is lightweight, open source and available on F-Droid.

Widgets Pro.desc: A collection of Nothing OS-style widgets (Android 12+): a music player that works with most players, sun tracking, a sports widget and, with Shizuku, CPU usage and temperature. It also lets you add GIFs from your gallery.
Widgets Pro.tip: If the widgets do not update, turn off battery optimization for the app.

Photo Widget.desc: Turns images from your gallery into widgets, with plenty of style customization. It does not work with GIFs.

L.L.E.desc: Brings the classic lock screen effects (Legacy Lockscreen Effects) to modern phones: lens flare, water ripples, watercolor, tiles, colored drops and shiny bubbles. It is compatible with foldables, with separate outer and inner screens. It needs the accessibility service and ADB to be installed.
L.L.E.tip: It is in beta and may crash. Use the 32-bit APK if your phone supports it.

Kvaesitso.desc: Open-source launcher where search comes first: apps, contacts, files, calendar, calculator and more from a single bar, with widgets and many ways to customize it.

Lawnchair.desc: Customizable launcher inspired by the one on Pixel phones, with themed icons, app drawer, gestures and settings everywhere. Open source (GPL-3.0).

Olauncher.desc: Text-only launcher, with no ads or distractions, designed to help you use your phone less: a home screen with few apps and gestures. Open source (GPL-3.0).

Muzei.desc: Changes your wallpaper automatically with artworks or your own photos, with blur and dimming so your icons stay easy to see. Open source (Apache-2.0).

Poweramp.desc: Excellent music player, with an advanced equalizer and a variety of highly customizable music widgets. It is closed source, so its privacy cannot be audited, and it is paid after the trial.

SpotiFLAC.desc: Open source, no ads and no subscription. Paste a playlist link or search by name and download in FLAC (lossless), Opus and other formats, depending on what each extension offers. Music sources are added with extensions.
SpotiFLAC.tip: First: in the Store tab, paste the «Extensión» link and then install the extensions with one tap. If a song is not found, turn on more providers in Settings > Extensions. Use it only with content you can legally download.

WEcho.desc: Applies audio effects to all system sound, not just one player: 1 to 64-band equalizer, compressor, bass boost, reverb, limiter and simulation of other headphones using the AutoEQ database. Works without root, and with Shizuku it improves compatibility. Open source (GPL-3.0). Android 10+.
WEcho.tip: arm64 only. The «Echo» AI agent needs your own language model key.

ClassiPod.desc: Player for the music stored on your phone with the iPod Classic design. Open source.

Helio.desc: Free music sequencer for composing: pattern editor, SoundFont instruments, exotic scales and version control to sync your projects between devices. Open source (GPL-3.0). Android 5+.
Helio.tip: It is for creating music, not for playing it.

Ambient Music Mod.desc: Brings «Now Playing» from Pixel phones to other Android devices: it recognizes background music with a local database, with history, favorites, a widget and manual recognition. It can show the song on the lock screen. It needs Shizuku (Android 12+) or the Sui module for Magisk (Android 9+). Android 9+ (11+ recommended).
Ambient Music Mod.tip: With Shizuku you have to start it again after every reboot. To show the song on the lock screen, it asks for an accessibility service.

Auxio.desc: Fast local music player with a clean design: it organizes your library by artists, albums and genres, reads the tags of your files and plays without gaps between songs. No ads or accounts. Open source (GPL-3.0).

ArchiveTune.desc: Alternative YouTube Music client with a Material You interface: it plays in the background, shows lyrics, downloads songs and saves your library, without using the official app. Open source.
ArchiveTune.tip: It is unofficial: it may break when YouTube Music changes something internally.

Gramophone.desc: Lightweight offline music player with a Material You style: it reads .mp3, .flac, .ogg, .opus, .m4a, .mka and .wav files, shows .lrc lyrics, picks colors from the cover art and supports SD cards. Open source (GPL-3.0).
Gramophone.tip: It only plays what you have on your phone: it does not download or stream.

LeanType.desc: Open-source keyboard based on HeliBoard: customizable themes and layouts, floating keyboard, one-handed mode and clipboard with history. Its core is offline; AI is optional and sends text to external providers only if you turn it on (there are versions without network access).

Irregular Expressions.desc: A very basic keyboard, but it offers different text fonts so you can type with style, something that is usually provided by Play Store apps with trackers.

GifBoard.desc: Search and share GIFs from the keyboard without leaving the app. It comes with its own QWERTY keyboard for searching, search history and adjustable columns and vibration.
GifBoard.tip: Heads up: it uses Google image search, so it depends on that service.

HeliBoard.desc: Free keyboard that works without internet, based on AOSP/OpenBoard: themes and colors to your liking, dictionaries for suggestions, clipboard history, multilingual typing and customizable layouts. Open source (GPL-3.0).
HeliBoard.tip: It does not include swipe typing: it needs a separate library, because there is no compatible open-source one.

FlorisBoard.desc: Free, modern keyboard with themes, one-handed mode, clipboard with history, emoji search and gesture typing. Open source (Apache-2.0).
FlorisBoard.tip: It is still under active development and may have bugs.

Simple Keyboard.desc: Lightweight keyboard (under 1 MB) with no ads: adjustable height, number row and your own colors, and it only asks for the vibration permission. Open source (Apache-2.0).
Simple Keyboard.tip: It has no emojis, GIFs, spell checker or swipe typing.

Fedora Linux.desc: Free, up-to-date Linux distribution, backed by Red Hat. Its Workstation edition comes with GNOME and is good for everyday use and for programming.

Linux Mint.desc: Linux distribution based on Ubuntu, designed for people coming from Windows: classic desktop (Cinnamon), everything ready to get started and lots of stability.

Qubes OS.desc: A system that separates each task into its own virtual machine («qubes»), so if one gets infected, the others stay safe. Open source.
Qubes OS.tip: It needs a powerful computer and quite a lot of patience to learn.

GrapheneOS.desc: Hardened, open-source Android focused on privacy and security: each app is isolated, you control permissions in more detail and it does not include Google services by default.
GrapheneOS.tip: In practice it can only be installed on Pixel phones. Back up everything first: installing it erases the phone.

LineageOS.desc: Free ROM based on Android for a huge number of phones. It is useful for giving years of updates to a phone that the manufacturer has already left behind, without Google apps out of the box.
LineageOS.tip: Unlocking the bootloader erases the phone: back up first and follow the guide for your model on their website.
